chapter: Teaching programs, mentors, White House and other bands
title: George Russell's importance and learning tunes quickly with Wes
summary: Baker calls the Russell band the biggest event in his career and says playing with Wes Montgomery meant learning five tunes before a gig.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: – was playing. He was on – he played in the Last Tango in Paris. He played in the music. Anyway, he was a Scandinavian, maybe a Norwegian, maybe from Norway. I don't remember. The George Russell thing was probably the biggest single event in my career, toward furthering the career. Playing with Wes [Montgomery] and those guys all the time, I felt like I was in very fast company from the beginning, because with Wes, and with Slide, and with those guys, you were ready to go to New York when you played with them, just because you had to really play to be able to even survive, because you had to learn music quickly. [When] you played with Wes, we’d play a park or something, and Wes would teach us five tunes before we would go on stage. The only problem you would have, you wouldn’t remember the head [the melody] when it came time to take it out. So Wes would have to play the head the first time through, so you could remember it.
